callers.name: Ada
callers.who: Harbor's first administrator: Access admin and Area manager at the root, so she holds every permission in harbor.
callers.connection: SELECT set_config('role', 'authenticated', false), set_config('request.jwt.claims', '{"sub":"<Ada>","role":"authenticated",…}', false), …, set_config('tenancy.caller_tenant', '<harbor>', false);

callers.name: Juno
callers.who: A seat at North Coast with no role of the organization; a surveyor on Pier 7's crew, which gives no permission to manage it.
callers.connection: SELECT set_config('role', 'authenticated', false), set_config('request.jwt.claims', '{"sub":"<Juno>","role":"authenticated",…}', false), …, set_config('tenancy.caller_tenant', '<harbor>', false);

callers.name: A new sign-in
callers.who: Signed in, with no seat in harbor.
callers.connection: SELECT set_config('role', 'authenticated', false), set_config('request.jwt.claims', '{"sub":"<the new sign-in>","role":"authenticated",…}', false), …, set_config('tenancy.caller_tenant', '', false);

callers.name: Orla
callers.who: One of the application's operators: her token carries the operators' role, and she has no seat anywhere.
callers.connection: SELECT set_config('role', 'tenancy_operator', false), set_config('request.jwt.claims', '{"sub":"<Orla>","role":"tenancy_operator",…}', false), …, set_config('tenancy.caller_tenant', '', false);

callers.name: Anonymous
callers.connection: SELECT set_config('role', 'anon', false), set_config('request.jwt.claims', '{"role":"anon"}', false), …, set_config('tenancy.caller_tenant', '', false);

callers.name: System work
callers.who: System work in harbor, started by trusted code with `access.BeginSystemIn(harbor)`.
callers.connection: SELECT set_config('role', 'ddd_system_in', false), set_config('request.jwt.claims', '{"role":"ddd_system_in","scope":"tenancy"}', false), …, set_config('tenancy.caller_tenant', '<harbor>', false);

scenarios.summary: Lists the units the caller reads. Requires a seat in the tenant.
scenarios.setSay: Each check says what it decides with a type test. `TenancyAccessCheck` says yes: `InTenant()` is a `TenancyRequirement`.

door.say: Ada has a seat in harbor, so `CurrentTenant.Require()` answers her tenant and seat.

statement.say: `InTenant` reads nothing in the access check. The host found the caller's seat in harbor when the request came in.

rows.say: The handler asks Tenancy's directory, which lists the units a seat is placed in and every unit below them. Ada is placed at the root, so all of them. Postgres asks `Members read the units` of each row: it is a unit of her tenant.

door.say: Juno has a seat in harbor.

statement.say: `InTenant` reads nothing in the access check. The host found the caller's seat in harbor when the request came in.

rows.say: Juno is placed at North Coast, which has no unit below it, so the directory lists one unit. Tenancy's policy is wider than the directory: it lets every member read every unit of the tenant, since the tree is the organization's and Tenancy's own questions read it as their caller.

door.say: No seat in harbor: the host found none for this identity, so the caller is nobody there, and `CurrentTenant.Require()` refuses with that reason.

statement.say: Nothing is sent: who the caller is was known before the request was sent.

rows.say: A statement they send directly reads no unit, because `caller_tenant()` finds no seat, so no row is in their tenant.

door.say: An operator has no seat anywhere: the operators' token role holds none, so she is nobody in harbor.

statement.say: Nothing is sent.

rows.say: Sent directly, she reads every unit of every tenant, because this policy lets operators read every tenant. The request requires a seat, while the table lets operators read. The access check and the policies answer different questions.

door.say: No token, so no seat.

statement.say: Nothing is sent.

rows.say: Sent directly, nothing is read. `anon` may not use Tenancy's schema at all, and a restrictive policy also closes every table in it.

door.say: System work in harbor works in the tenant: `CurrentTenant.Require()` answers harbor, by system work.

statement.say: `InTenant` reads nothing in the access check.

rows.say: For system work in the tenant the directory lists every unit. The connection runs as `ddd_system_in`, and the policy of system work keeps it to harbor.

scenarios.summary: Adds a unit below another. Requires tenancy.units.manage at the parent, or above it.
scenarios.setSay: `TenancyAccessCheck` says yes: `AtUnit(permission, unit)` is a `TenancyRequirement`. The core's check and Tenancy's check of operators say no, and are passed by.

door.say: Ada holds `tenancy.units.manage` at the root, and the root is above North Coast.

statement.say: One statement, as Ada. It joins her `SeatRights` rows to the closure table of the tree, so "at North Coast or above it" is one join.

rows.result: 200 · a new unit below North Coast
rows.say: The handler hands the request to Tenancy's use case, which asks for the permission again and writes the unit and its paths. Postgres asks the insert policy of the new row: the same permission, at the parent.

door.say: Meadow Gardens' root is not a unit of harbor, and Ada's permissions are harbor's only. The statement finds the permission at no unit above it. The refusal names the permission and the unit.

statement.say: One statement, as Ada. None of her permissions reaches that unit.

rows.say: Sent directly, the insert policy refuses the row. The row is not in her tenant, and its parent is not one of the units where she holds the permission.

door.say: Juno holds `tenancy.units.manage` nowhere. The refusal names the permission and the unit.

statement.say: One statement, as Juno. It finds no permission.

rows.say: Sent directly, the insert policy refuses the row. The parent is not in `units_where_i_hold_permission('tenancy.units.manage')` for her.

door.say: The check asks the caller first: nobody in harbor is refused with its own reason.

statement.say: Nothing is sent: the check asks the caller first, and a caller that is nobody in harbor is refused before a statement is made.

rows.say: Sent directly, the insert policy finds no tenant of theirs, and refuses the row.

door.say: An operator is nobody in harbor, and is refused before anything is read.

statement.say: Nothing is sent: the check asks the caller first, and a caller that is nobody in harbor is refused before a statement is made.

rows.say: Sent directly, the insert fails before any policy is checked. No permissive policy lets the operators' role write Tenancy's units, so the role has only `SELECT` there, the one command its policy here allows.

door.say: No token, no seat: refused before anything is read.

statement.say: Nothing is sent: the check asks the caller first, and a caller that is nobody in harbor is refused before a statement is made.

rows.say: Sent directly, nothing is written. `anon` may not use Tenancy's schema, and a restrictive policy closes every table in it.

door.say: System work in harbor holds every permission there, at a unit of harbor, and North Coast is one.

statement.say: One statement all the same: whether North Coast is a unit of harbor.

rows.result: 200 · a new unit below North Coast
rows.say: Written as `ddd_system_in`, scope `tenancy`: the policy of Tenancy's own work lets it write rows of its own tenant.

outcomes.row: System work, below Meadow Gardens' root

door.say: Every permission, but only at a unit of its own tenant: Meadow Gardens' root is not harbor's.

statement.say: One statement: whether that unit is harbor's. It is not.

rows.say: Sent directly, the policy for Tenancy's work refuses a row of another tenant, because `system_tenant()` is harbor.

scenarios.summary: Puts a seat on a project's crew. Requires projects.crew.manage on that project.
scenarios.setSay: `MemberAccessCheck<Project, ProjectId>` says yes: `On(permission, project, version)` is a `MemberAccess<ProjectId>`. Tenancy's two checks say no to it, though they are earlier in the set.

values.label: Bay bridge, Juno not on it

door.say: Ada may act: she holds `projects.crew.manage` from above. Only then is the version compared, and somebody changed the project since she read it. A caller who may not act never learns that.

statement.say: One statement, as Ada: the project, how she holds the permission, and its version.

rows.say: The handler does not run. Read the project again, and decide again.

outcomes.row: Ada, either project, the version she read

door.say: Ada holds `projects.crew.manage` at the root, and the projects' rules let a permission held where a project sits count on the project: from above.

statement.say: One statement, as Ada, built from the projects' rules: the project as she sees it, how she holds the permission, and its version. What it read is kept for the save.

rows.result: 200 · the seat is on the crew
rows.say: The handler loads the project, admits the seat, adds it and saves. Postgres asks the crew's policies of the new row: a permissive one for whoever may change the project, and Membership's restrictive lock, which asks for the permission that changes the members.

door.say: Juno sees Pier 7, she is on its crew, but a surveyor's role gives no `projects.crew.manage`. The refusal names the permission. The version is not compared: she may not act.

statement.say: One statement: a row comes back, with no way of holding the permission.

rows.say: Sent directly, Membership's lock refuses her row. Pier 7 is not in `projects_where_i_hold('projects.crew.manage')` for her.

door.say: Juno reaches Bay bridge in no way: not on its crew, not its owner, no permission where it sits. For her it does not exist, as a project of another tenant does not.

statement.say: One statement: no row comes back.

rows.say: Sent directly, Membership's lock refuses her row as well.

door.say: Membership asks the caller first: a crew member is a seat, and Tenancy's answer for nobody is its own refusal.

statement.say: Nothing is sent: the check asks the caller first, and a caller that is nobody in harbor is refused before a statement is made.

rows.say: Sent directly, the crew's policies find no seat of theirs, and refuse the row.

door.say: An operator is nobody in harbor, and is refused before anything is read.

statement.say: Nothing is sent: the check asks the caller first, and a caller that is nobody in harbor is refused before a statement is made.

rows.say: Sent directly, the insert fails before any policy is checked, because her role has only `SELECT` on the crew's table. Tenancy's restrictive `Operators only read` would refuse the row as well.

door.say: No token, no seat: refused before anything is read.

statement.say: Nothing is sent: the check asks the caller first, and a caller that is nobody in harbor is refused before a statement is made.

rows.say: Sent directly, nothing is written. No permissive policy is for `anon`, so it may not use the schema of a module that belongs to a tenant, and a restrictive policy also closes every table in it.

door.say: System work holds every permission, so only the project and its version are read. The version is not the one it read.

statement.say: One statement: the project and its version, nothing about permissions.

rows.say: The handler does not run.

outcomes.row: System work, the version it read

door.say: The projects' own work, in their scope, holds every permission on every project.

statement.say: One statement: the project and its version, nothing about permissions.

rows.result: 200 · the seat is on the crew
rows.say: Written as `ddd_system_in`, in the projects' scope: the policy of system work in its tenant lets it add a member to a project of harbor, and Membership's lock lets through the scope the projects' rules name. Work in Tenancy's scope would hold nothing on a project.

scenarios.summary: Gives a seat another name: your own, or any with tenancy.seats.manage for the whole tenant.
scenarios.setSay: An `Any` is decided by the set, case by case: `Own(seat)` by the core's check, `AtTenant(permission)` by Tenancy's. Both must have a check before either is asked.

door.say: The first way in holds: the seat the request names is Ada's own in harbor. The permission is not asked.

statement.say: Nothing is sent. The access check compares the caller's own seat with the seat found when the request came in.

rows.say: The handler loads the seat and renames it. The update policy lets a seat change its own row, and the column rule on the name lets a seat change its own name.

door.say: Not her own seat, so the second way in is asked: `tenancy.seats.manage` for the whole tenant, which she holds at the root.

statement.say: One statement, for the second way in: the permission at harbor's root.

rows.say: The update policy lets a holder of `tenancy.seats.manage` change any seat's row, and the column rule on the name asks the same permission for the whole tenant.

door.say: Her own seat: the first way in.

statement.say: Nothing is sent.

rows.say: The policy and the column rule both let a seat change its own name.

door.say: Neither way holds: not her own seat, and no `tenancy.seats.manage`. One `access.refused` carries both reasons, `access.not-own` and `tenancy.not-permitted` with the permission.

statement.say: One statement, for the second alternative. It finds no permission.

rows.say: Sent directly, the update policy hides Leo's row from her, so the statement changes nothing.

door.say: No seat in harbor, so no seat of their own; and the permission's way refuses nobody in harbor with its own reason. Both reasons, `access.not-own` and `tenancy.not-seated`, in one `access.refused`.

statement.say: Nothing is sent: the caller's own reads nothing, and the permission's way refuses nobody first.

rows.say: Sent directly, the update policy finds no seat of theirs in harbor, so it lets them change no row. The statement changes nothing.

door.say: No seat in harbor, so no seat of their own; and the permission's way refuses nobody in harbor with its own reason. Both reasons, `access.not-own` and `tenancy.not-seated`, in one `access.refused`.

statement.say: Nothing is sent: the caller's own reads nothing, and the permission's way refuses nobody first.

rows.say: Sent directly, neither may change a seat. No permissive policy lets the operators' role write Tenancy's seats, so the export grants it only `SELECT` there, and Postgres refuses the update before it checks a policy. `anon` may not use Tenancy's schema at all. The column rule on the name would refuse both roles as well.

door.say: System work has no seat of its own, so the first way in refuses; it holds every permission in harbor, so the second lets it through, with nothing read.

statement.say: Nothing is sent: system work in the tenant holds every permission there.

rows.say: Written as `ddd_system_in`, allowed by the policy for Tenancy's own work. The column rule checks only the roles of callers, so system work passes it.

scenarios.summary: Reads a tenant's audit log: an operator, or the permission that manages seats for the whole tenant.
scenarios.setSay: An `Any` of two of Tenancy's cases: the set gives `Operator()` to Tenancy's check of operators and `AtTenant(permission)` to `TenancyAccessCheck`, in that order.

outcomes.row: Orla, with the operators' rule forgotten

door.say: The first way in holds: her token's role is an operator's.

statement.say: Nothing is sent: the operators' case reads the token's role.

rows.say: The trap. The access check let her through, but with the operators' rule gone no permissive policy is for her role. The Supabase export writes a table's privileges from its permissive policies, so `tenancy_operator` may not read the audit table at all. The read fails with 42501, permission denied. The toolkit does not turn this error into a refusal, so the host answers 500. When the host grants the privileges itself, she reads an empty page instead, with no reason given. Each alternative of an `Any` that reaches a table of your own needs its own row rule.

door.say: The first way in holds: her token's role is an operator's. The permission is not asked.

statement.say: Nothing is sent: the operators' case reads the token's role.

rows.say: The handler reads the tenant the request names. The operators' rule lets her role read every tenant's rows, and gives it its one privilege on the table, `SELECT`; Tenancy's restrictive `Operators only read` refuses every row it would write as well.

door.say: Not an operator, so the first way in refuses, with `tenancy.operators-only`. The second holds: `tenancy.seats.manage` for the whole tenant.

statement.say: One statement, for the second way in.

rows.say: The seat managers' rule lets her read the rows, and Tenancy's restrictive policy keeps them to her tenant.

door.say: Neither way: `tenancy.operators-only`, then `tenancy.not-permitted` for the permission. One `access.refused`, with both.

statement.say: One statement, for the second alternative. It finds no permission.

rows.say: Sent directly, the seat managers' rule lets her read no row, because she does not hold the permission.

door.say: Neither way: `tenancy.operators-only`, and `tenancy.not-seated`. One `access.refused`, with both.

statement.say: Nothing is sent: neither way reads anything for a caller who is nobody in harbor.

rows.say: Sent directly, the seat managers' rule lets them read no row. No seat of theirs manages seats, and Tenancy's restrictive policy finds no tenant of theirs.

door.say: Neither way: `tenancy.operators-only`, and `tenancy.not-seated`. One `access.refused`, with both.

statement.say: Nothing is sent: neither way reads anything for a caller who is nobody in harbor.

rows.say: Sent directly, nothing is read. No permissive policy is for `anon`, so the export grants it nothing. It may not read the table, nor use its schema.

door.say: Not an operator; the second way holds: system work holds every permission in harbor, with nothing read.

statement.say: Nothing is sent: system work in the tenant holds every permission there.

rows.say: Read as `ddd_system_in`, allowed by the policy that Tenancy writes for system work on every table that belongs to a tenant. That policy keeps it to harbor.

scenarios.summary: Makes a new tenant with the caller as its first administrator. Requires a signed-in person.
scenarios.setSay: The core's `CurrentUserAccessCheck`, first in every set, says yes: `SignedIn()` is about who is calling, and means the same in every module.

outcomes.row: Ada or Juno, the system work forgotten

door.say: Signed in: the token names a user.

statement.say: Nothing is sent: `SignedIn()` reads the token.

rows.say: The access check let them through, but the handler started no system work. Tenancy's provisioning refuses a seat with `access.system-only`. Who may send a request and which caller the work runs as are two separate decisions.

outcomes.row: the new sign-in or Orla, the system work forgotten

door.say: Signed in: the token names a user. An operator is a signed-in user too.

statement.say: Nothing is sent: `SignedIn()` reads the token.

rows.say: The handler began no system work, and the provisioning refuses a caller with no seat with that caller's own reason.

outcomes.row: Ada, Juno, the new sign-in, Orla

door.say: Signed in: the token names a user. An operator is a signed-in user too.

statement.say: Nothing is sent: `SignedIn()` reads the token.

rows.result: 200 · a new tenant, the caller its administrator
rows.say: The handler reads the administrator from the caller's own token, then begins system work outside any tenant. The provisioning moves on to system work in the tenant it makes, so every row it writes is that tenant's. After the `using` the next statement runs as the caller again.

door.say: No token names a user.

statement.say: Nothing is sent.

rows.say: Sent directly, no policy lets a caller write a tenant. Only Tenancy's own work may, in the tenant whose id the connection names.

door.say: System work is nobody's sign-in. Work only trusted code does needs no request at all: it calls the use case inside the scope, as the sample's seeding provisions its tenants.

statement.say: Nothing is sent.

rows.say: Only Tenancy's own work outside any tenant provisions, and only for the tenant whose id the connection names.

// ... the module's other lines, and a last arm that answers the module's default, TenancyAccess.InTenant()
public async ValueTask<TResponse> Handle(TMessage message, MessageHandlerDelegate<TMessage, TResponse> next, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
// CurrentUserAccessCheck, the core's, shortened: who is calling, with nothing read
=> requirement is AccessRequirement.SignedInUser || (requirement is IOwnedRequirement owned && owned.CanBeAnswered(services));
if (!user.IsAuthenticated)                               // a token that names a user
case IOwnedRequirement owned:                                // the request names the value, never whose it is
public bool Decides(AccessRequirement requirement) => requirement is TenancyRequirement && !IsOperatorCase(requirement);
access.CurrentTenant.Require();                          // a seat here, or system work here
access.CurrentTenant.Require();                          // nobody is refused without a statement
throw new InvalidOperationException("... which Tenancy's access check does not decide ...");
// MemberAccessCheck<Project, ProjectId>, Membership, the case of a permission on a project, shortened
public bool Decides(AccessRequirement requirement) => requirement is MemberAccess<ProjectId>;
var hold = await access.RequireAsync(required.Resource, required.Permission, cancellationToken);
//   nobody                         -> the caller's own refusal, tenancy.not-seated
//   does not see the project       -> projects.not-found
//   sees it, does not hold the permission -> projects.not-permitted
kept.KeepFor(request, hold);                                 // what the save is held to
// CombinedAccessCheck, the core's, shortened: Any lets the first case that holds decide
try { await Require(each, request, cancellationToken); return; }   // the first that lets the caller through
throw ToolkitRefusals.NoneMet(reasons);                      // one access.refused, every reason in it
await Require(each, request, cancellationToken);         // in order; the first refusal is the answer
-- HoldsAtTenantAsync: the permission at the tenant's root, approximately what Entity Framework sends
INNER JOIN "tenancy"."OrganizationUnits" AS root ON r."UnitId" = root."Id"
WHERE r."TenantId" = @tenant AND r."SeatId" = @seat AND r."Permission" = @permission
AND r."StartsAt" <= @now AND (r."EndsAt" IS NULL OR r."EndsAt" > @now)
AND root."TenantId" = @tenant AND root."ParentId" IS NULL)
-- HoldsAtAsync: the permission at the unit or above it, approximately what Entity Framework sends
INNER JOIN "tenancy"."OrganizationUnitPaths" AS p ON r."UnitId" = p."AncestorId"
WHERE r."TenantId" = @tenant AND r."SeatId" = @seat AND r."Permission" = @permission
AND r."StartsAt" <= @now AND (r."EndsAt" IS NULL OR r."EndsAt" > @now)
-- HoldsAtAsync for system work in the tenant: every permission there, at a unit of the tenant, approximately
SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM "tenancy"."OrganizationUnits" AS u WHERE u."TenantId" = @tenant AND u."Id" = @unit)
-- EfMemberQuestions.HoldAsync: the project as the caller sees it, and how the permission is held, approximately
EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM "projects"."ProjectCrewMembers" AS m                 -- on the crew now,
AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM "projects"."ProjectCrewRoleGrants" AS h   -- in a role that gives the permission
INNER JOIN "projects"."ProjectRoles" AS k ON h."RoleId" = k."Id"
WHERE h."CrewMemberId" = m."Id" AND k."Status" = 'Active' AND @permission = ANY (k."Permissions")))
OR p."OwnerSeatId" = @seat AS "AsMember",                                 -- or its owner
p."UnitId" IN (SELECT path."DescendantId" FROM "tenancy".caller_permissions() AS r   -- or the permission where it sits
INNER JOIN "tenancy".tenant_unit_paths() AS path ON r."UnitId" = path."AncestorId"
AND (/* the caller sees it: on the crew, its owner, or projects.view where it sits */)
-- no row: projects.not-found; a row whose AsMember and FromAbove are both false: projects.not-permitted
-- EfMemberQuestions.HoldAsync for system work: every permission, so only the project and its version
SELECT p."Version" FROM "projects"."Projects" AS p WHERE p."Id" = @project LIMIT 1
CREATE POLICY "Members read the units (select) for authenticated" ON "tenancy"."OrganizationUnits" FOR SELECT TO authenticated
CREATE POLICY "System work reads its tenant (select) for ddd_system_in" ON "tenancy"."OrganizationUnits" FOR SELECT TO ddd_system_in
CREATE POLICY "Operators read every tenant (select) for tenancy_operator" ON "tenancy"."OrganizationUnits" FOR SELECT TO tenancy_operator
CREATE POLICY "Unit managers add below their units (insert) for authenticated" ON "tenancy"."OrganizationUnits" FOR INSERT TO authenticated
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION "tenancy".units_where_i_hold_permission(permission text) RETURNS SETOF uuid
LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = '' AS $function$
JOIN "tenancy"."OrganizationUnitPaths" p ON p."AncestorId" = r."UnitId" AND p."TenantId" = r."TenantId"
AND r."StartsAt" <= pg_catalog.now() AND (r."EndsAt" IS NULL OR r."EndsAt" > pg_catalog.now())
CREATE POLICY "Tenancy work writes its tenant (insert) for ddd_system_in" ON "tenancy"."OrganizationUnits" FOR INSERT TO ddd_system_in
CREATE POLICY "Closed to anonymous callers (all) for anon" ON "tenancy"."OrganizationUnits" AS RESTRICTIVE FOR ALL TO anon
CREATE POLICY "Managers and the seat change it (update) for authenticated" ON "tenancy"."Seats" FOR UPDATE TO authenticated
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION "tenancy".seats_displayname_column_rule() RETURNS trigger

IF ((OLD."Id" = (SELECT "tenancy".caller_seat())) OR (SELECT "tenancy".holds_at_tenant('tenancy.seats.manage'))) IS NOT TRUE OR (OLD."Id" IS DISTINCT FROM NEW."Id" AND ((NEW."Id" = (SELECT "tenancy".caller_seat())) OR (SELECT "tenancy".holds_at_tenant('tenancy.seats.manage'))) IS NOT TRUE) THEN

RAISE EXCEPTION USING ERRCODE = 'insufficient_privilege', CONSTRAINT = 'seats_displayname_column_rule', HINT = 'ddd:access.refused', MESSAGE = 'The column rule ''Name changes by the seat or with the seats permission'' does not let this caller change "DisplayName" of "tenancy"."Seats".';

RAISE EXCEPTION USING ERRCODE = 'insufficient_privilege', CONSTRAINT = 'seats_displayname_column_rule', HINT = 'ddd:access.refused', MESSAGE = 'No column rule is for this caller''s role, so it may not change "DisplayName" of "tenancy"."Seats".';
CREATE TRIGGER seats_displayname_column_rule BEFORE UPDATE OF "DisplayName" ON "tenancy"."Seats"
FOR EACH ROW WHEN (OLD."DisplayName" IS DISTINCT FROM NEW."DisplayName")
